Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

circuitscaper 0.2.0

New features

  • cs_setup(threads = ) now restarts Julia when it is already running with fewer threads (or with an interactive thread, which breaks parallel runs of Omniscape < 0.6.3), instead of warning that R must be restarted.
  • If the Julia process stops during a session (for example, it crashes or runs out of memory, or is stopped with JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()), the next circuitscaper call starts and sets up Julia again, instead of failing with connection errors until R is restarted.

Bug fixes

  • circuitscaper now runs Julia in its own process, connected to R by ‘JuliaConnectoR’, instead of inside R’s process via ‘JuliaCall’. With Julia inside R, the libraries R had loaded clashed with the ones Julia bundles, and setup failed on Linux: on Ubuntu 24.04, Julia’s GDAL could not load because terra had already loaded the system libtiff (“version LIBTIFF_4.6.1' not found"), and Julia could also crash on the system libunwind. 'JuliaConnectoR' also starts Julia without R'sLD_LIBRARY_PATH, which crashed Julia's package manager. Julia packages are likewise installed in a separate Julia process with a clean library path. RCall.jl is no longer needed, and the…argument ofcs_setup()(passed toJuliaCall::julia_setup()`) is gone.

  • The shell and Julia commands circuitscaper runs to find and check Julia (including at package attach) now time out instead of potentially hanging, e.g. on a slow login shell profile.

  • cs_setup() and cs_install_julia() now refuse Julia versions older than 1.10 with an explanation of how to upgrade. On older Julia, the package manager falls back to old releases of Circuitscape.jl and Omniscape.jl that fail in obscure ways. The minimum in SystemRequirements is now Julia 1.10.

  • cs_install_julia() now downloads and installs Julia itself, from the official release index at julialang.org, verifying each download against its published size and (on R >= 4.5) SHA-256 checksum. Julia goes into circuitscaper’s user data directory (tools::R_user_dir("circuitscaper")) and is found automatically by cs_setup(). Previously it used JuliaCall::install_julia(), which in the current CRAN release of ‘JuliaCall’ (0.17.6) installs Julia 1.9 when asked for the latest version and can’t install Julia 1.10 or later, so a fresh install failed with errors such as “undefined symbol: SET_SYMVALUE”.

  • cs_setup() now starts the Julia it finds explicitly, so the Julia whose version it checks is always the one that starts, and stops with a clear message if an older Julia is already running in the session.

  • cs_setup() now finds Julia wherever JuliaCall::julia_setup() would, instead of only on the PATH. Previously, a Julia installed by cs_install_julia() (which JuliaCall::install_julia() places outside the PATH) was not found in later sessions, so cs_setup() failed with “Julia not found” until julia_home was given explicitly. The same applied to Julia installed via juliaup or Homebrew when R was started from the macOS GUI, whose PATH lacks the shell’s. cs_install_julia(), cs_julia_available(), and the startup message use the same search.

  • os_run(parallelize = TRUE) now checks the running Julia session before calling Omniscape, and warns and runs serially if it cannot run in parallel: if Julia has only one thread, or if it was started with an interactive thread (e.g. JULIA_NUM_THREADS = "4" rather than "4,0"), which makes Omniscape releases before 0.6.3 fail with a BoundsError. This can happen when Julia is started outside cs_setup(), for example by another package.

  • cs_setup() now records the number of threads Julia actually has, and warns when threads cannot take effect because Julia was already running (including when started outside circuitscaper). Previously it recorded the requested count, and os_run(parallelize = TRUE) could reset the record to 1 when it started Julia.

  • os_run() now has Omniscape write its outputs as ASCII grids rather than GeoTIFFs. Writing GeoTIFFs from Julia could crash R (seen on Ubuntu, in TIFFClose), most likely because Julia’s GDAL loads its own libtiff into a process where R’s terra has already loaded the system one. Inputs were already passed as ASCII grids, so Julia now never touches libtiff. Files kept via output_dir are therefore .asc rather than .tif.

  • os_run() now stops with a clear error if the resistance or conductance surface contains zero or negative values, which Omniscape rejects without writing outputs. Previously this surfaced as an obscure failure to read Omniscape’s output.

circuitscaper 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-10-01

New features

  • New os_condition() constructor gives os_run() full access to Omniscape’s conditional connectivity (#2):
    • "within" comparisons with user-specified bounds (lower, upper).
    • Present-vs-future comparisons (future), in which sources’ present-day values are compared against targets’ future values, as in climate-tracking connectivity analyses.
    • Two simultaneous conditions, by passing a list of two os_condition() objects.
  • os_run() now warns when a condition layer has missing values at source cells, which Omniscape does not filter.
  • All cs_*() functions and os_run() now warn if the installed Circuitscape.jl or Omniscape.jl does not recognize a configuration option written by circuitscaper, rather than letting the option silently have no effect.

Bug fixes

  • In 0.1.0, os_run()’s condition_type argument was written to the Omniscape configuration under a key Omniscape does not recognize, so it was silently ignored. All conditional analyses instead used Omniscape’s defaults, "within" with bounds of 0 and 0: a source was connected to a target only if its condition value exactly equaled the median value of the target block. This was neither the documented behavior (an unbounded range) nor the requested "equal" comparison. Results from 0.1.0 that used condition should be rerun.
  • In 0.1.0, four_neighbors = TRUE was written to the Circuitscape configuration under an unrecognized key and silently ignored in cs_pairwise(), cs_one_to_all(), cs_all_to_one(), and cs_advanced(); all analyses used 8-neighbor connectivity. Results from 0.1.0 that used four_neighbors = TRUE should be rerun.

Breaking changes and deprecations

  • Passing a raster directly as os_run(condition = ) is now shorthand for os_condition(x, type = "equal"). Use os_condition() for "within" comparisons, which now require explicit bounds.
  • os_run()’s condition_type argument is deprecated. condition_type = "equal" still works with a warning; condition_type = "within" now errors, since it has no way to specify bounds.
